summary.text: A halophile is an extremophile that thrives in high salt concentrations; most are archaea, but some are bacteria or eukaryotes.
They live in places like the Great Salt Lake, the Dead Sea and evaporation ponds, where salt can exceed five times the ocean's.
Salty water tends to pull water out of their cells, so they raise their internal osmolarity by gathering organic compounds or absorbing potassium (K⁺) ions.

facts.label: Extreme halophiles
facts.value: Prefer 3.4 to 5.1 M salt, or 20 to 30%

facts.label: Color
facts.value: Some give off a red color from carotenoid compounds

items.prompt: A technician washes salt-lake microbes in pure distilled water. What happens to many of them?

options.label: They burst, due to the sudden change in osmotic conditions
They multiply faster in the cleaner water
They go dormant and wait for salt to return
They grow larger and turn red

items.explain: Many halophiles are so fragile that in distilled water they immediately lyse from the change in osmotic conditions.

items.prompt: A microbe grows in brine but does just as well in fresh water. How should it be described?

options.label: A halophile, since it can grow in brine just fine
An extreme halophile, since brine is what suits it
An osmophile, since it is adapted to high sugar levels
Halotolerant, since it can grow in salty conditions without needing them

items.explain: Halophiles require salt for growth, while halotolerant organisms do not require it but can grow under saline conditions.

items.prompt: Why is absorbing potassium the more radical of the two ways to survive salt?

options.label: It forces the cell to shed most of its cytoplasm first
It requires the cell to stop using its enzymes altogether
All the cell's internal enzymes and structural proteins must be adapted to high salt
It only works for a cell that is kept away from light

items.explain: The potassium strategy needs the entire intracellular machinery adapted to high salt, whereas compatible solutes need little or no adjustment.

items.prompt: Which group usually makes up most of the prokaryotes in very salty lakes and ponds?

options.label: Salinibacter ruber bacteria
Haloarchaea
Dunaliella salina algae
Wallemia fungi

items.explain: Haloarchaea comprise the majority of the prokaryotic population in hypersaline environments, while bacteria are commonly a much lower share.

items.prompt: Isolation studies of salt ponds keep turning up the same genus again and again. What caution applies?

options.label: The genera easiest to isolate may be rare in the natural community
The genus must be the most common one there
Isolation studies always match natural populations
The genus must be a bacterium rather than an archaeon

items.explain: Haloarcula commonly appears in isolation studies but is estimated at under 0.1% of the in situ community.

items.prompt: Why do biologists who think about Jupiter's moon Europa care about salt-loving microbes on Earth?

options.label: They have already been found living in Europa's ice
They may be a model for microbes in Europa's salty subsurface ocean
They are the only microbes that can survive freezing
They are the same species as ones living on Europa

items.explain: Halophiles are theorized to be possible analogues for extremophiles that might live in the salty subsurface ocean of Europa.
